previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, diastolic heart failure, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for worsening bilateral leg swelling, foul-smelling drainage from chronic ulcers, and subjective fevers. She had gained approximately 20 pounds recently and reported orthopnea and dyspnea on exertion. Elevated BNP and pulmonary congestion on imaging confirmed acute exacerbation of diastolic heart failure, managed with IV furosemide and transition to daily oral torsemide. She was treated for left lower extremity cellulitis with IV vancomycin, later transitioned to oral linezolid for a full 14-day course. Wound culture grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa, but it was deemed colonizing rather than infective. She improved clinically, lost over 10 kilograms, and was discharged home on stable medications with follow-up plans. INR was subtherapeutic on admission but normalized with continued warfarin. No DVT was found on Doppler ultrasound.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Presence of right artificial knee joint
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism

FINDINGS: 

Osseous structures are diffusely demineralized.  No concerning lytic or
sclerotic osseous abnormalities detected.  No periosteal new bone formation or
cortical destruction is present.  Severe tricompartmental degenerative changes
of the knee are demonstrated with joint space narrowing, osteophyte formation,
and subchondral sclerosis.  Diffuse soft tissue swelling is present without
soft tissue gas.  There are scattered soft tissue calcifications, likely
vascular in etiology.  A moderate size plantar calcaneal spur is noted, with a
well corticated fragment noted distally.  No acute fracture or dislocation is
present.  The ankle mortise is symmetric.  Mild tibiotalar degenerative
changes are seen including subchondral cysts within the talar dome medially. 
Moderate degenerative changes are noted within the midfoot.

IMPRESSION: 

No definite radiographic evidence for osteomyelitis.  Diffuse soft tissue
swelling without soft tissue gas.  Please note that MRI with contrast is more
sensitive for detection osteomyelitis.
